statement: You are given a string s and a dictionary of words wordDict, written as one comma-separated string.
Return true if s can be split into a sequence of one or more dictionary words, with nothing left over. A word may be used more than once.

This version stores the dictionary in a trie. dp[i] records whether the first i letters of s can be split. From every position i where dp[i] is true, walk the trie along s[i], s[i + 1], …; each time the walk reaches the end of a word at position j, set dp[j + 1] to true. The answer is dp[n], where n is the length of s.

examples.explanation: s splits into "leet" and "code", both in the dictionary.
"cats" or "cat" can start the split, followed by "and" or "sand", but that leaves "og", which no word matches.

constraints: s and the dictionary words consist of lowercase English letters.
